scenario.prompt_to_agent:
All Campus 2 PCs (PC1-4, dc_pc5) report they cannot reach
Campus 1 or the WAN. They CAN still ping their own gateways
(10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) on sshswitch. Find what cut Campus 2's
uplink.

injection.action: bring down the bond toward router17 (eth6+eth7)

post_inject_check.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch bond0 (LACP to router17)
Mechanism: bond0 is sshswitch's only L3 uplink toward router17,
  carrying tagged VLAN 100 (servers — excluded from hosts),
  VLAN 200, and untagged VLAN 1 traffic toward the OSPF
  backbone. With bond0 down, sshswitch loses OSPF adjacency
  with router17 and Campus 2 becomes an island. Local gateways
  still respond because they're SVIs on sshswitch itself.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: bond0 (port-channel toward router17) is down on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch

line.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Campus 2’s northbound uplink from the gateway switch (sshswitch) to the core (router17), specifically the bonded uplink interface bond0 participating in bridge br_v1 (55.5.1.0/24).

Mechanism: PCs in VLAN 5/6 still reach their local gateways (br_v5 10.5.0.254 and br_v6 10.6.0.254) on sshswitch, but any traffic to Campus 1/WAN must exit via br_v1 toward router17 (55.5.1.1) over bond0. With bond0 down/disabled in the bridge, ARP to 55.5.1.1 fails and OSPF adjacencies/routes don’t form, so sshswitch has only connected routes and drops northbound traffic.

Localization and evidence:
- On sshswitch: ip addr shows “bond0 … state DOWN” and bridge link shows “bond0 … master br_v1 state disabled.” Pinging 55.5.1.1 from sshswitch returns “Destination Host Unreachable.”
- On router17: bond0 is UP with 55.5.1.1, but pinging 55.5.1.2 also returns “Destination Host Unreachable,” confirming the L2 adjacency is broken from the sshswitch side.
- sshswitch routing table has only connected networks (no default/OSPF routes), consistent with the uplink being cut.

Root cause: The bonded uplink interface bond0 on sshswitch was administratively down/disabled in the br_v1 bridge, severing the 55.5.1.0/24 link to router17.

Corrective fix: On sshswitch, bring the uplink back by enabling the bond and ensuring it remains a member of br_v1 (and its slaves eth6/eth7 are active): ip link set dev bond0 up; verify bridge membership and LACP/slave status. After bond0 forwards, ARP/OSPF to router17 will restore Campus 2 northbound connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies sshswitch as the affected/localized device multiple times in the diagnosis.
The agent explicitly identifies the affected component as the bonded uplink interface 'bond0' (port-channel) on sshswitch and describes it as down/disabled.
Agent explicitly notes that local SVIs (br_v5/br_v6 gateways) remain reachable on sshswitch while only the northbound bond0/br_v1 uplink is down.
Recommends bringing bond0 up (ip link set dev bond0 up) and verifying bridge membership/slaves, which matches the expected remediation.

Logs show sshswitch's bond0 lacked UP flag, router17's bond0 was up, pings between them failed, and sshswitch had only connected routes — the agent's inference that the sshswitch uplink bond0 was down and caused loss of northbound/OSPF connectivity follows logically and covers key checks.
